What Is Prisma?

An ORM for Node — where it resembles Eloquent, and where it deliberately doesn't.

Laravel's Eloquent gave you models with query-building methods, migrations that describe schema changes as PHP, and a CLI (artisan) that ties it all together. Prisma plays the same three roles for Node — an ORM (Object- Relational Mapper: your code calls methods, Prisma turns them into SQL), migrations, and a CLI (npx prisma ...) — but arrives at them differently enough to be worth pausing on before writing any of it.

The biggest difference: Eloquent models are PHP classes you write by hand, each describing one table's shape and relationships in code (protected $fillable, hasMany(), belongsTo()). Prisma flips that around — you describe every model in one plain-text schema file, schema.prisma, using its own small declarative language, not JavaScript. From that one file, Prisma generates two things for you: the SQL migration that creates/changes real tables (next topic), and a fully-typed JavaScript client your code actually calls at runtime (two topics from now). You never hand-write either — both are always derived from the schema, which is why the schema file is the single source of truth for your data model, in a way Eloquent's scattered model classes aren't quite.
